rules._note: Set 11/19/2026 from the backtest lab (docs/data/lab.json, walk-forward 2024-2027; see the CBB Model project's backtest-findings doc). Only big edges vs OPENING lines made money; everything loses vs the close, so bet early. Totals: unders only (10+ unders 160-113 +11.9% vs openers; overs lost). Spreads: 10+ pt edge = A (11/20, after the v2 model: 10+ vs openers +19.1%, up every season; 7-10 dropped to +1.3%). Moneylines lost -6.1% and the model's win% runs ~10 pts high: never official. Props: unchanged, being graded live. Grade: tier points + matchup (props) - 1 if the line moved against us; 2+ = A, 0-1 = B, <0 = C. A line moving our way never raises a grade; it adds a 'bet small' tag (CFB lesson). Props (11/25, Rod): Points props can't be A (lost in the backtest week -12% and live -7.9%); a prop priced -150 or worse can't be A (juice ate the A's edge: 56.4% hit vs 55.9% needed). Capped plays drop to B.

model._note: Which model the lab and the live run use. Change only after run_backtest.py --compare shows it is better vs BOTH opening and closing lines. 11/19/2026: v2 (3-point luck, roster/transfers, availability, schedule; props carry last season) beat base on every headline number (feature_test.json). The anchored variant matched the market almost exactly (good win% calibration, but no betting edge), so it stays off.
